## Why visit

The tiny rooms and miniature servery make this one of the most distinctive traditional-pub experiences in the centre. It is worth visiting for the intimacy of the surviving beerhouse layout, not for a large beer range. Sit down if invited and let the setting dictate a slower pace. Combined with neighbouring Grey Horse, it offers an enjoyable comparison of two very small Manchester pubs. Avoid building a plan around arriving exactly at opening time: the current specialist listing explicitly cautions that hours can vary.

## Beer

CAMRA documents two cask beers; choose for the pub experience rather than breadth of selection.

## Plan the visit

Very limited space; table service is described by CAMRA. Opening and closing can vary with trade, so keep a nearby alternative.

**Getting there:** Central Portland Street; walk from Piccadilly Gardens or Oxford Road and combine with Grey Horse.

Check [November transport issues](../logistics.md) for date-specific disruption.
